record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Can gravitational-wave measurements distinguish sub-solar-mass PBH binaries from neutron stars, white dwarfs, or exotic compact objects by using tidal disruption and tidal deformability Λ constraints, so that a sub-solar compact-binary merger can be interpreted as a primordial-black-hole signal rather than another compact-object population?

evidence.quote: The detection of sub-solar BHs in a compact binary merger is regarded as one of the smoking gun signatures of PBHs. Indeed, BHs of astrophysical origin are not expected.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a compact binary merger detected through gravitational waves whose component masses are inferred to lie in the sub-solar regime (below approximately one solar mass). Candidate constituents in this mass range include primordial black holes (PBHs), low-mass neutron stars, white dwarfs, and exotic compact objects such as boson stars. A black hole has vanishing (dimensionless) tidal Love number, so its tidal deformability parameter Λ is zero, while material/exotic compact objects generically possess Λ > 0 with magnitudes determined by their internal equation of state, and they can also undergo tidal disruption during inspiral.

Develop a quantitative gravitational-wave inference framework that uses (i) waveform constraints on the tidal deformability Λ of each binary component and (ii) the presence or absence of tidal-disruption features in the late inspiral/merger to determine whether a sub-solar compact-binary merger signal can be statistically distinguished as a PBH–PBH binary from binaries containing neutron stars, white dwarfs, or exotic compact objects. Specifically:

1. Determine, as a function of detector network sensitivity (e.g. current and next-generation ground-based interferometers), component masses, and signal-to-noise ratio, the confidence level at which model-agnostic upper bounds on Λ derived from a sub-solar event can exclude neutron-star and exotic-compact-object hypotheses.
2. Establish whether tidal-disruption signatures and Λ measurements together are sufficient to positively identify a sub-solar merger as originating from primordial black holes, rather than merely excluding alternatives.
3. Quantify residual degeneracies (e.g. exotic objects with arbitrarily small Λ) that may prevent an unambiguous PBH identification.
artifact.category_tag: Primordial black holes and gravitational-wave tidal signatures
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has developed concrete tidal-deformability tests for sub-solar gravitational-wave events, showing that during the LIGO/Virgo O4 run a sub-solar PBH binary could be distinguished from a neutron-star binary at roughly 3σ using model-agnostic Λ bounds, and follow-up papers extend this to exotic compact objects (e.g. boson stars, "tidal gap" causality bounds). Thus the question is partially solved—forecasts and methodology exist and exclusion of neutron stars looks feasible—but a fully model-independent identification of PBHs against all exotic-compact-object alternatives remains open, since exotic objects with arbitrarily small Λ can mimic black holes.

status_evidence.title: Can we identify primordial black holes? Tidal tests for subsolar-mass gravitational-wave observations
status_evidence.snippet: For subsolar PBH binaries, O4 projected sensitivity would allow ruling out the presence of neutron-star tidal effects at approximately 3 sigma confidence level, thus strengthening the PBH hypothesis.
status_evidence.claim: Tidal-deformability measurements can statistically distinguish sub-solar PBH binaries from neutron-star binaries during O4.

status_evidence.title: Primordial black holes versus their impersonators at gravitational wave observatories
status_evidence.snippet: Distinguishing PBHs from impersonators (boson stars, exotic compact objects) using GW signatures.
status_evidence.claim: Distinguishing PBHs from exotic-compact-object impersonators is an active and not fully resolved program.

status_evidence.title: The tidal gap: causality bound on exotic compact objects with applications in the solar and sub-solar mass range
status_evidence.snippet: Causality-based 'tidal gap' between black holes and exotic compact objects.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical bounds on exotic-object tidal deformability are still being developed, indicating partial progress.
